findings.statement: Partly fixed, still open. The new paragraph reads as a complete list of the design §9 agent choices that the design approval endorses, but it names only six. ADR-0006 restates at least four more §9 agent choices, and those still sit unmarked under owner-decision headings: (a) §9 bullet 7, the 'N exclue(s)' counter limited to explicit refusals, appears in D9 at lines 121-122 ('counts only the destinations the matched rules explicitly deny'); (b) §9 bullet 2, authenticated link delivery of media, appears in D6 at lines 81-83; (c) §9 bullet 6, a revision becomes a comment, appears in 'Fan-out and idempotency' at line 192; (d) §9 bullet 11, the new destination-disclosure-leak predicate rather than a new meaning for public-data-leak, appears at lines 233-236 and 257. The ADR-0005 amendment says its origin is 'owner decisions D8 and D10', but it also carries §9 bullet 5 (the popup delegates preparation to the editor, chunked delivery, the service worker holds nothing) without marking it. The list also names 'the refusal of non-conforming instances', which no part of the ADR body records.
findings.evidence: design §9 (spec lines 511-528) has 11 bullets. ADR-0006:44-48 lists WASM, author/approver separation, the typed origin, token profiles, no managed browser policy, and refusal of non-conforming instances. Running `grep -n -i 'non-conforming' ADR-0006` returns only line 48. ADR-0006:81-83, 121-122, 192, 233-236 and 257 restate §9 bullets 2, 7, 6 and 11 without the marker. ADR-0005 amendment: '- Origin: owner decisions D8 and D10', then 'The editor prepares the delivery anew' and 'The service worker holds neither key nor bytes.' Fix: either extend the paragraph to cover every §9 choice the ADR restates and drop the one it does not record, or mark each such sentence where it appears.

findings.statement: This predates the bd822bd fixes; pass 1 missed it. The ADR header attributes the supersession of design §5.5 to '2026-10-24 owner decisions ... recorded in roadmap §4.2, §4.5 and §6'. The only §5.5 change is the rule that an unreadable visibility withholds the destination (reason visibility-unknown). Roadmap §4.2 records that rule in its 'Visibilité illisible' bullet, which is not labelled as an owner decision. In §4.2 only the rule precedence carries 'décision propriétaire du 2026-10-24'. The same change rewrote the design (§5.5 and §9 bullet 1), and that rewrite replaced an agent choice endorsed by the design approval ('lecture en échec traitée comme publique'). Severity is minor because the change is stricter, matches the approved §7 test ('une lecture de visibilité en échec fait retenir'), and comes from a roadmap the owner merged (signalement PR #23, merged 2026-10-24T06:23:08Z by constantin-jais). Still, Q5 asks for corrections that apply recorded owner decisions only, and the ADR presents a roadmap clarification as an owner decision.
findings.evidence: ADR-0006:9-10: 'they supersede design §5.2 point 5, §5.5 and §5.6 where they differ'. roadmap:211 labels only the 'Précédence des règles (décision propriétaire du 2026-10-24)'. roadmap:214-216, the 'Visibilité illisible' bullet, has no owner label. Spec diff 950135d...HEAD changes §5.5 ('Une lecture en échec retient tous les fichiers...') and §9 bullet 1. Fix: in the ADR header, name the visibility rule as a roadmap §4.2 clarification that aligns §5.5 with the approved §7 test, not as an owner decision, or have the owner label it.

findings.statement: Introduced by the fixes. The new test 'no v1.0 provider row is verified before its qualification' arrives in commit bd822bd without the two gate-integrity answers: what concrete error turns it red, and whether an equivalent refactor would turn it red. The commit records no neutralization run either. The earlier commits of this branch (04369ae, 721acc1) record both for their tests. By inspection the test does discriminate: setting any of the four rows to `verified` fails `expect(row?.status).not.toBe("verified")`. The test does not freeze the `unresolved` status, which matches the F7 ruling.
findings.evidence: `git log -1 --format=%B bd822bd` contains no gate-integrity questions and no red run. Commit 04369ae's message includes 'Gate-integrity questions: 1. ... (test 1, measured red) ... 2. A refactor would not turn them red'. Fix: state both answers and the neutralization result in the PR description or a follow-up commit message.

limitations: Q1: pass, except for F5 and F8. D4 to D13 each appear in ADR-0006, and each consequence matches design §4: D4 'product core'; D5 shared engine, refined by D11; D6 imposed/optional/selectable/override; D7 the export is unchanged and the receipt follows §5.5; D8 scripting through the active tab; D9 the count only; D10 the observed origin; D11 one source of state; D12 one key per deployment and roles from OIDC; D13 projection only, under usable-verifiable.

Q2: pass. ADR-0005:66 contains the design §5.2 phrase word for word: 'voluntary active-tab capture, observed origin retention, and gesture-bound delivery to one configured origin'. The phrase occurs once on that single line (`grep -c` = 1). The original line 45 is kept as history.

Q3: pass. The new criteria policy-routing, signed-receipt-offline, gesture-bound-delivery and stale-plan-refused, the extended two-real-profiles and browser-matrix-real, and the predicate destination-disclosure-leak match design §7 and roadmap §5 exactly, case included. All are `pending`. 'status: accepted' appears 3 times at 950135d and 3 times at HEAD. maturity (specified) and exposure (spec-published) are unchanged.

Q4: pass. The four v1.0 provider rows are `unresolved`, and each statement opens with its exact profile id (github-issues/github.com/rest-2022-11-28, gitlab-issues/gitlab.com/rest-v4, jira-cloud/cloud/rest-v3, plane/self-hosted/rest-v1). After the F1 fix, the only new `verified` assumption row (gitlab-project-token-tier) holds a documentation fact plus a recorded owner decision. The new decision-lock rows are `verified` in the file's existing sense ('decision recorded in an ADR'). Observation, not a finding: ADR-0006 and the ADR-0005 amendment now call themselves 'proposed' until the owner's merge, so these rows cite a source that calls itself proposed. They take effect in the same merge, and this follows the ADR-0055 precedent that the controller ruled on: ADR-0055 is still 'proposed' at its merge commit and is registered as D94.

Q5: pass, except for F8. The design status matches merged ADR-0055: PR #134, merge commit 84c0e6d634cc845452bddf7864977547b1a96455, merged 2026-10-23T07:03:02Z by constantin-jais, register line 100 'D94 ... ADR-0055 — 2026-10-23'. The Annex A quote matches ADR-0055 D1. The §5.2 point 5 correction and the §5.6 GitLab correction apply the owner decisions in roadmap §4.5 and §6. The §5.6 Jira correction applies a documentation measurement recorded in roadmap §6, through the design's own fallback ('sinon à résoudre').
Q6: pass. Neither the diff nor the commit messages add a dated Owner-arbitration marker. The only added match is the prose 'n'écrit jamais de ligne `Owner-arbitration:`'.

The reviewer did not re-read the external documentation behind the 2026-10-24 measurements (the GitLab project access token page, Atlassian search and reconcile): those tools fall outside the allowed command set. This review qualifies no provider, browser or deployment.
I did not exercise test neutralization, because this review is read-only. The test in F9 is judged to discriminate by inspection only.
This review is not owner consent or owner arbitration. Under their own status lines, ADR-0006 and the ADR-0005 amendment take effect only when the owner merges the PR.
I did not read the implementers' reports or the per-lot plan files. The references were the design (HEAD and 950135d), the roadmap, ADR-0055 and the pass-1 review.
